seo.title: SQL editor with autocomplete and EXPLAIN
seo.description: Write SQL with schema-aware autocomplete. Save queries, search local history and inspect EXPLAIN plans on supported databases.

header.title: SQL editor
header.lead: Write SQL with schema-aware autocomplete. Save queries you reuse, search your history and inspect plans on supported engines.

sections.title: Schema-aware autocomplete
paragraphs: Autocomplete suggests tables and columns, including aliases, CTEs and subqueries. Format the current statement with <kbd>⌘⇧L</kbd> while keeping its comments.

Run the current statement, a selection or a whole script. Ordinary statement batches use one transaction and roll back on failure. SQL Server scripts, explicit transactions and statements such as VACUUM are exceptions. DDL on MySQL, MariaDB and Oracle commits independently.
points: Statement markers in the gutter, each with its own run button.
Find and replace, with regular expressions.
Vim mode with motions, registers and macros, where :w runs the query.
.sql files open, edit and save as query tabs.

sections.title: Parameters, history and saved queries
paragraphs: Use parameters such as :customer_id to enter values before a query runs. Values are bound natively where the driver supports it.
Search local query history by text, source, failures or time range. It keeps {historyEntries} entries for {historyDays} days by default and never syncs.

Save queries with reusable keywords and version history. Link a folder of .sql files to the sidebar with two-way updates and Git status. Linked SQL folders are free, separate from the paid Linked Folders feature for connection files.

sections.title: Open Quickly and tabs
paragraphs: Open Quickly (<kbd>⌘⇧O</kbd>) searches tables, views and queries across open connections. Tabs retain their SQL and grid settings when you reopen the app.

blocks.title: EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN Compare
paragraphs: View query plans as diagrams, cost trees or raw engine output. Compare with an earlier run to spot timing and plan changes; differences under {explainNoise}% count as noise. Both features are free.

engines.label: Plan as a diagram and tree

blocks.title: Query Insights
paragraphs: Find slow, failing and frequently run queries in this Mac's local history. Similar statements are grouped regardless of parameter values. Query Insights compares periods locally; it is not server-wide monitoring and uploads no metrics.

sections.title: Results as charts and maps
paragraphs: A result can switch from the grid to a chart or a map in the same tab, and back.

blocks.title: Result Charts
paragraphs: Plot results as bar, line, area or scatter charts. Charts show up to {chartPoints} points and {chartSeries} series from the first {chartInspectedRows} rows, with a notice when truncated.

blocks.title: Map view
paragraphs: View supported geometry columns on Apple Maps and select a shape to find its row. Rows stay on your Mac; Apple supplies the map tiles. Map view is free.

sections.title: Other query languages
paragraphs: Use each non-SQL engine's query language in the editor. MongoDB uses a built-in mongosh-style JavaScript shell, not mongosh itself. See the database pages for supported commands.

sections.title: On iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The iPhone and iPad app has a Query tab with SQL highlighting, Run and Stop (<kbd>⌘↩</kbd> with a keyboard), and a history of the last {historyEntriesIos} queries run on that device. You can copy or share a result as JSON, CSV or SQL INSERT statements.
It has no autocomplete, formatting, parameters, EXPLAIN or saved queries, and it holds at most {resultBufferIos} rows of a result, so add a LIMIT to see the slice you need.

availability.label: SQL editor with autocomplete and formatting
availability.iosNote: Highlighting, Run and Stop; no autocomplete

availability.label: Query history
availability.iosNote: The last {historyEntriesIos} queries on the device

availability.label: Saved queries and linked SQL folders

limits: A query returns at most {rowCap} rows unless you raise the cap in Settings, up to {rowCapMax}, or run it with <kbd>⌘⌥⏎</kbd>. A LIMIT you write yourself always wins.
Query history and Query Insights cover this Mac only: queries run on another Mac or on iPhone are not in them.
The tablepro shell command opens connections and files in the app. It does not run queries from the terminal.
